title: Cadence Orchestrator: RC catalog + SLA-aware rollout fanout
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a cadence orchestrator that produces a catalog of weekly RCs, attaches SLA-facing rollout policies (canary cohort + regional fanout), and wires an automated release-notes composer that summarizes visible regressions and SKUs impacted.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Produce an authoritative RC catalog (metadata: semver candidate tag, base commit, model of included changes, expected latency delta bucket) after each weekly cut.
- Attach rollout policy templates to each RC: canary cohort definition (percent, shard keys), SLA gates (error budget thresholds, p99 latency limits), and automatic fallback triggers.
- Release notes automation: generate human-friendly changelogs from conventional commits, merged PRs, and runtime telemetry diffs (latency/cost deltas) and publish draft to Confluence and a GitHub release.
- Rollout orchestration must integrate with Console feature flags and routing to enable staged fanout across regions and Dedicated pools.
- Testing: synthetic canaries, A/B traffic split harness, and smoke checks tied to SLO dashboards within 15 minutes of deployment.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Semver policy: weekly cuts will create candidate versions using YY.MM.Wx semantics (e.g., 25.02.W2-rc.1) to emphasize cadence over micropatch numbers; LTS lanes will be pinned to patch numbers with explicit backports. This reduces version churn for users on stable channels.
- SLA gating granularity: prefer conservative, per-route p99 and 5m error-rate windows to avoid noisy rollbacks; more aggressive signals (tail-latency heatmaps) will be used as advisory metrics in the release notes.
- RC catalog storage: lightweight JSON manifest stored in the releases S3 bucket with immutable naming; index is pushed to the Console catalog API for consumption by deployment services.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Catalog generator: script that collects PR metadata, changelog entries, runtime diff snapshot, and writes manifest to s3 + Console API.
2) Rollout templates: YAML policy definitions for canary cohorts + gating thresholds; default templates for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
3) Orchestrator service: small controller that reads catalog entries and executes staged fanout using routing API and Console feature flags.
4) Release notes composer: lambda that synthesizes conventional-commit changelogs, picks highlight bullets from merged PR descriptions, and appends quick telemetry summary (p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token estimate).
5) Runbook and rollback: automated playbook that can revert routing or pin to previous RC; include incident checklist and postmortem links.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement model-level quantization recommendations or automatic model variant substitution policies; those are out of scope and will be separate epics.

Open questions:
- Should telemetry diffs be computed by comparing the RC baseline to the most recent GA candidate or to the previous RC? (Current leaning: compare to previous RC for cadence transparency.)
- How granular should the canary cohorts be for Dedicated pools with heterogeneous GPU types?

Acceptance test notes:
- End-to-end weekly cut run in the staging environment that produces an S3 manifest, Console catalog entry, and a drafted Confluence release note.
- Orchestrator successfully rolls out the RC to a 5% canary cohort in eu-central and triggers a simulated failure to validate automatic fallback to previous RC within 3 minutes.

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Cadence+Orchestrator+Design (draft)
- Draft runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1-Cadence-Orchestrator-Runbook
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/812
- Canary harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rc-canary-harness
